-Heroines design mostly on point
-Good potential
-Horror side adds a lil bit of creativity/mystery.

Bad:
-Feels like there's 10x more effort put into the "horror" scenes than the sex scenes.

posts.content_html_raw:
Disclaimer: many of these will be my creative writing

First, the whole event has 4 segments: red room, rabbit living room, Sensei's room raising a flower baby, and the abandoned school with a cross we've seen before. The focus is placed a lot more on the first two segments and I severely lack ideas regarding the latter two.

Red room
A scene quite faithfully reconstructed from Twin Peaks. I don't necessarily think Himawari is dead by the time of this event just like how Laura Palmer was in the TV series (what does death mean to a shapeshifting unborn daughter anyway). As in, I think what is directly applicable here instead is "someone in the left chair is looking for something", and "a certain girl in the right chair has the answer". What Sensei wants to know is what happened to the rest of the beach trip according to what Moyo alludes to, and the message Himawari whispers brings us to the next scene where this beach trip is more addressed.

There are other foreboding words from both Moyo and Himawari in between that aren't directly from Twin Peaks:
  • H: At this rate you'll miss your ride
  • M: Halloween is coming
  • H: Something is right around the corner and it could catch if you keep this up (thought it was talking about Halloween for a sec)
  • M: You wouldn't want to miss "that extra pair of legs", and everyone that misses all looks a lot like you and they're all in the clouds now.
I have no idea whether Moyo and Himawari here are finishing each other's sentences or simply talking about their own separate things. If the both of them are on the same topic, then Sensei's existence might soon be in danger like how Sensei himself interprets it. Endangered by what exactly isn't all that clear for the time being. A reset? A certain entity? A certain girl? "That extra pair of legs" alone isn't enough for my imagination to go off. Besides, IF the both of them are on the same topic, that means you want to be caught in order to not end up in clouds when normally it's the other way around, and this is the part I don't get it at all.

Rabbit living room
(someone let me know if this is another reference to some other famous show)
This scene is played before Sensei (the one that has ??? as name not the one that has Sensei as name) walks in, but this scene here because Himawari enables it by asking his dad to relay words to the rabbits. Thus I'd like to think that this scene contains roundabout answers to Sensei's original question that is "what happened during the beach trip". By piecing up the conversations we can get "the beach is canceled but not all of it" and "What happened on the beach was an accident".

With the amount of doomsaying in this update, I'd like to think that a reset was supposed to take place on the beach according to the time schedule and the fact that RAS is attempting to actively research information again (though I take this with a grain of salt), but then something went wrong on the world's side. The reset is either failed, incomplete, or aborted, limiting its mind-correcting effect to those in proximity. This is currently my only explanation to why Yumi's perception is spared but not Sana's without going into "Yumi being a lot more special". In all honesty, it doesn't have to be a reset judging from how different this incident is compared to other resets, and it can be just another fuckery we have or haven't seen before, but it regardless is a fuckery that might not have proceeded as planned or even unintended.

And I subjectively make the mental connection between "fuckery not working" with "the key looks a little different this time". This implies that a certain item/condition/something can be repeatedly recognized and used/met/obtained for a reoccurring purpose, but not this time.

Sensei's room raising a flower baby
This scene reminds me of Bioshock Infinite so much, a familiar room in grayscale that exists only in jumbo memories, a cradle, and a father-daughter pair. This might be resonating to Himawari's origin as a part of the secrets she whispers into Sensei's ears, or this might be an aftermath of Sensei forgetting to tell rabbits about the her birthday crown, but it's too cryptic to say anything with high confidence.

Abandoned school with a cross we've seen before
Classic LiL pretentious BS. Not a clue about where it could be fitted or if it's trying to say something specific.

Finally a dancing Moyo for everyone because I am going crazy thinking about this (that's me when the leak dropped)

spoilers.title: An attempt to understand 0.42 happy event
spoilers.html:
Disclaimer: many of these will be my creative writing

First, the whole event has 4 segments: red room, rabbit living room, Sensei's room raising a flower baby, and the abandoned school with a cross we've seen before. The focus is placed a lot more on the first two segments and I severely lack ideas regarding the latter two.

Red room
A scene quite faithfully reconstructed from Twin Peaks. I don't necessarily think Himawari is dead by the time of this event just like how Laura Palmer was in the TV series (what does death mean to a shapeshifting unborn daughter anyway). As in, I think what is directly applicable here instead is "someone in the left chair is looking for something", and "a certain girl in the right chair has the answer". What Sensei wants to know is what happened to the rest of the beach trip according to what Moyo alludes to, and the message Himawari whispers brings us to the next scene where this beach trip is more addressed.

There are other foreboding words from both Moyo and Himawari in between that aren't directly from Twin Peaks:
  • H: At this rate you'll miss your ride
  • M: Halloween is coming
  • H: Something is right around the corner and it could catch if you keep this up (thought it was talking about Halloween for a sec)
  • M: You wouldn't want to miss "that extra pair of legs", and everyone that misses all looks a lot like you and they're all in the clouds now.
I have no idea whether Moyo and Himawari here are finishing each other's sentences or simply talking about their own separate things. If the both of them are on the same topic, then Sensei's existence might soon be in danger like how Sensei himself interprets it. Endangered by what exactly isn't all that clear for the time being. A reset? A certain entity? A certain girl? "That extra pair of legs" alone isn't enough for my imagination to go off. Besides, IF the both of them are on the same topic, that means you want to be caught in order to not end up in clouds when normally it's the other way around, and this is the part I don't get it at all.

Rabbit living room
(someone let me know if this is another reference to some other famous show)
This scene is played before Sensei (the one that has ??? as name not the one that has Sensei as name) walks in, but this scene here because Himawari enables it by asking his dad to relay words to the rabbits. Thus I'd like to think that this scene contains roundabout answers to Sensei's original question that is "what happened during the beach trip". By piecing up the conversations we can get "the beach is canceled but not all of it" and "What happened on the beach was an accident".

With the amount of doomsaying in this update, I'd like to think that a reset was supposed to take place on the beach according to the time schedule and the fact that RAS is attempting to actively research information again (though I take this with a grain of salt), but then something went wrong on the world's side. The reset is either failed, incomplete, or aborted, limiting its mind-correcting effect to those in proximity. This is currently my only explanation to why Yumi's perception is spared but not Sana's without going into "Yumi being a lot more special". In all honesty, it doesn't have to be a reset judging from how different this incident is compared to other resets, and it can be just another fuckery we have or haven't seen before, but it regardless is a fuckery that might not have proceeded as planned or even unintended.

And I subjectively make the mental connection between "fuckery not working" with "the key looks a little different this time". This implies that a certain item/condition/something can be repeatedly recognized and used/met/obtained for a reoccurring purpose, but not this time.

Sensei's room raising a flower baby
This scene reminds me of Bioshock Infinite so much, a familiar room in grayscale that exists only in jumbo memories, a cradle, and a father-daughter pair. This might be resonating to Himawari's origin as a part of the secrets she whispers into Sensei's ears, or this might be an aftermath of Sensei forgetting to tell rabbits about the her birthday crown, but it's too cryptic to say anything with high confidence.

Abandoned school with a cross we've seen before
Classic LiL pretentious BS. Not a clue about where it could be fitted or if it's trying to say something specific.

Finally a dancing Moyo for everyone because I am going crazy thinking about this (that's me when the leak dropped)

Himawari is not dead, but she is also not truly alive. In her own words during this scene, she has not yet worn her "birthday crown" This is a reference to "crowning," or the passage of the head through the birth canal. So her being the parallel to Laura Palmer is actually quite fitting, because at their respective points in their stories, neither are alive.

Further, the third part of the story - Sensei raising infant Himawari alone for 3 weeks -- would imply that something happens to Ayane during childbirth. Not necessarily death (as we're given a specific time frame), but something that prevents her from being present for that time.

Speculation: The reset was supposed to happen, but got cancelled because something that the powers WANTED to happen was going to happen or had just happened, and the powers didn't want to rewrite that knowing it may not happen in a subsequent run, so they did a partial rollback instead. If I had to guess, it was the Yumi scene that prompted the adjustment.

Speculation, part deux: Between the comments in Futaba's scene about the ones who fail their tasks becoming angels and the line about "in the sky now" and "looks a lot like you" would imply that this rule applies to Sensei as well, which means all of the failed Senseis likely become Angels

Himawari is not dead, but she is also not truly alive.  In her own words during this scene, she has not yet worn her "birthday crown" This is a reference to "crowning," or the passage of the head through the birth canal.  So her being the parallel to Laura Palmer is actually quite fitting, because at their respective points in their stories, neither are alive.
Further, the third part of the story - Sensei raising infant Himawari alone for 3 weeks -- would imply that something happens to Ayane during childbirth.  Not necessarily death (as we're given a specific time frame), but something that prevents her from being present for that time.
Speculation: The reset was supposed to happen, but got cancelled because something that the powers WANTED to happen was going to happen or had just happened, and the powers didn't want to rewrite that knowing it may not happen in a subsequent run, so they did a partial rollback instead.  If I had to guess, it was the Yumi scene that prompted the adjustment.
Speculation, part deux: Between the comments in Futaba's scene about the ones who fail their tasks becoming angels and the line about "in the sky now" and "looks a lot like you" would imply that this rule applies to Sensei as well, which means all of the failed Senseis likely become Angels

posts.content_html_raw:
Okay, full 0.42 thoughts.

I'm so glad to see this friendship surviving. Ami certainly needs it. Although I still can't tell with her. She seems genuine? That's the easiest thing to believe but she's also capable of just uping the layers of deception for Ayane. Maybe I'm paranoid. Ayane at least thinks she's still being weird but maybe that's just how honestly looks on her?

A lot of people like Maya, and while she's never been one of my favorites, I do miss Maya Prime. Maya Prime was so aware and composed. I thought her insults were funny and her presense did feel comfortable as she was a sort of guiding character. New Maya is energetic, more talkative, and sort of oblivious. She certainly acts younger. Thinking back to an early happy event, New Maya does act like she did in that hidden 2nd reset event on the rooftop. She feels like a new character and that's enforced by resetting her affection.

Kirin has one line in this update, but I gotta say I'm starting to like Kirin a lot. There might be one similarity between Sensei and I in that we both want people to stand up to him. I don't know what she can do to him but she a least has a sharp tongue and she's fairly smart. I thought the last update might be the end of this conflict but it seems that's not the case. Good for her.

Quoting a person who, as Wakana put it, "preaches madness" and saying you look up to them is not a good look, Otoha. -5 me affection.

Just an observation. Miku might be the friendliest person in the cast. She gets along with EVERYONE.

I tried so hard to think it through as I read but... I don't get it. We did get a ton of new info though. Also do we really not get a follow up on what happened from the volleyball players' perspective? Futaba just suddenly vanished.

GAHHH This relationship is so sweet. This is the stuff I live for. Uta says she'll never abandon Io and would give up Sensei for her if she wanted. They're both in a confusing spot atm so they have some things to work out but these two might just have the most unbreakable relationship in this game. Not that this game wont eventually go in that direction...
...
Please don't go in that direction

I thought the detentions were before the loop. I still think they were pre-loop but it would be consistent if remembering the other slumber party meant remembering things she shouldn't in general.

CHIKKKAAA. We knew something like this was going to happen sooner or later. And now is later. Much later. While the specifics are kind of tame, this is much worse than her walking in on someone imo. Sensei says he'll talk to Chika but ultimately ghosts her instead. The reason he gives is that he doesn't deserve forgiveness but that's probably just an excuse to be a coward. He completely ignores her. She's left to wallow in self doubt and worry. She finds him flirting with Yumi, says this is the whole reason he came, and returns to his room with her. Not only does he appear to be cheating, it's with her best friend and he couldn't even be bothered to at least pretend to care about his girlfriend.
I feel really bad for her. Honestly I have no idea how Chika is going to respond to this. I don't know how Yumi could explain it either as that last line from Sensei was VERY incriminating and "it was a time traveler meeting" obviously wont work.
She's supposed to be resilient so I doubt her response will be passive.

Now I gotta wait an entire month to see how this blows over. Her last known state is "bawling her eyes out" until then.

That was a good bonus event. She deserves it. Also carrying her comatose body back into the room was pretty funny. I'd love to know what they were all thinking.

Think Maya's different? Meet Sana. My god is she different.
ANOTHER THING. Why did we receive a picture message when she's one of the few girls whose number we don't have?

We miss ALL of Sunday??? ALL OF IT? What even happened? Why did Ayane need to leave if every else turned out okay?

Niki is kind of the perfect person to deal with Ami. Ami thrives in speaking between the lines. She has this strategy where she adds a layer of doubt to her suggestions so she can manipulate the conversation without ever reaching full on confrontation. Niki's bluntness cuts through that. She says exactly what she wants and what she's thinking. No beating around the bush.
Maybe Niki really is just what Ami needs? I don't think Ami is going to let this happen though. She'll play nice for Sensei's sake but no way is she going to just let Niki be Sensei's wife. She hinted as much in the first event. Especially when jealous Sekai is offering suggestions (wow she really got herself those pjs too).

This is a shot in the dark but I think Ami's best angle here is to find subtle ways to expose some of Sensei's relationships to Niki. Either Niki leaves or that girl does, which is a Win-Win for Ami.

This event had some good jokes. Some people say that Rika is unimportant but some lighthearted events surrounding all the trauma is pretty important. Rika exudes tomfoolery so I like her. It's also amazing that Rika is so weird she turns Imani into the straight man (In a non-sexual way). She's also surprisingly perceptive? Her gaydar doesn't go off on Yuki, which is right. She says Rin probably has a crush on Sensei, which is right. She suspects Sana and Sensei might be doing stuff, which is right. I wonder if this will continue to be a thing.

But this conversation also brings up that Imani is waaaay less aware of Sensei returning the student's affection than I thought. That might be catastrophic down the line.

Overall, a very good update!

She has this strategy where she adds a layer of doubt to her suggestions so she can manipulate the conversation without ever reaching full on confrontation. Niki's bluntness cuts through that. She says exactly what she wants and what she's thinking. No beating around the bush.
Maybe Niki really is just what Ami needs? I don't think Ami is going to let this happen though. She'll play nice for Sensei's sake but no way is she going to just let Niki be Sensei's wife. She hinted as much in the first event. Especially when jealous Sekai is offering suggestions (wow she really got herself those pjs too).

This is a shot in the dark but I think Ami's best angle here is to find subtle ways to expose some of Sensei's relationships to Niki. Either Niki leaves or that girl does, which is a Win-Win for Ami.

spoilers.title: Rika
spoilers.html:
This event had some good jokes. Some people say that Rika is unimportant but some lighthearted events surrounding all the trauma is pretty important. Rika exudes tomfoolery so I like her. It's also amazing that Rika is so weird she turns Imani into the straight man (In a non-sexual way). She's also surprisingly perceptive? Her gaydar doesn't go off on Yuki, which is right. She says Rin probably has a crush on Sensei, which is right. She suspects Sana and Sensei might be doing stuff, which is right. I wonder if this will continue to be a thing.

But this conversation also brings up that Imani is waaaay less aware of Sensei returning the student's affection than I thought. That might be catastrophic down the line.

There are two scenes that play if Ayane's affection is high enough. The first one is "scientific research" a main event in chapter 1. Akira goes to the beach and can spend time with Chika, Yumi or Chinami (or Himawari, if Ayane's affection is high enough).

You can only get this one through cheating though, and you'll get a cheater flag for it.

The second one is during the "miserably ever after" main event in chapter 4, where you can choose a 4th song if Ayane's affection is high enough, the songs starts playing a bit later. This doesn't give you a cheater flag, and it's one of the reasons people assume the narrator for the event is Himawari.

What has been said about the Sana scene at the beach is not based on Ayane's affection, but if you're having sex with Sara (iirc). It's either "ad meliora" or "ad infinitum".

If you view either event on replay and have URM, just choose the option when it pops up, there's no need to manually trigger either of the events. You will have to manually trigger "flowerchild" if you want to see Himawari at the end again, so the manually triggering is true for some cases, just not these ones.

They forgot about the second day at the beach, not the first.

The first day is saturday, and it is concluded by Sana stealing Akira from bed, and Himawari coming to save Ayane. From that point forward, things get reset. We don't get to see Sunday, which was about Akira having sex all morning and afternoon with Makoto, then having sex with Ayane before bed. We see them again on monday as they're leaving.

So, basically, it was sunday that was lost, and saturday got changed a little bit. We're on a different "timeline" where Sana did not get to learn about resets, and instead it was just Yumi. It's unclear from her text message if she still stole Akira away from bed, but if she did it had nothing supernatural about it.

I mean, it's not impossible for the reset to have been caused by Chika killing people, but it's also highly unlikely, when we had three different moons at the same time in front of Akira and Sana (who doesn't have anything to do with Chika). Also, the audio file states that they're changing things because understanding what was shown would cause a factory reset to many others, and it would be the end of Akira (which also doesn't have anything to do with Chika).
The most important point about all of this is that Himawari has a plan and we're about to see it come through. She tells Akira not to leave the room after telling him about gates (if she's the narrator), but he does anyway. Then she comes in to save Ayane, and later on monday after they leave the beach he finds her note in his pocket (second time she does this): "meet me in the spring time".

The issue with this is that this narrator always says stuff like "are you ready to meet me?" - and especially what she says about gates is that in her timeline she knows the harmony gate wasn't built, and that was either because she left, or because he did. My point is, Himawari has met Akira plenty of times. So either this narrator is someone else, or she means meeting her as she really is (outside of the simulation?)

There is also some woman with a suitcase that is familiar to Akira as he's going home (it would be wild if it was Ayane's mother). And the time that he spent with baby Himawari might have taken place during the lost day of the weekend since his clothes are still wet. But that's also a huge stretch. Anyway, don't burn your brains on this, it will get revealed soon and we'll finally grasp Himawari's plan.
Soon, with Halloween.

Edit: one minor thing that could be a huge thing is that Ayane asks Himawari if they're about to reset, and Himawari's answer is: "Reset?", like what the hell are you talking about/what even is that. I have no idea what to make of that. But I keep wondering now if resets are even a thing when it's been confirmed that they're slipping through planes. Maybe instead of resetting they're being sent to yet another kumon-mi each time? (like I needed even more complication).

First post! Long time listener, first time caller. Finally caught up with the game and, admittedly while I'm on the theory train, I'm more likely at the dumb dumb table. I read through the stuff on here about the 0.42 Happy Event and didn't see much about the David Lynch references so I thought I would kick some things around. The first part in the red room is from Twin Peaks, which was mentioned and is a whacky show and good watch for the most part...very 90s. In the show, the place is called the Black Lodge and takes place both inside the dreams of the main character, but is also a physical location with supernatural figures who are essentially playing a chess game within the town.

Second scene is David Lynch's Rabbits: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=drjQfQtv2BQ
David Lynch has said that any of his art is subjective and whatever interpretation the audience gets from it is always valid (something Selebus has parroted a few times in the Discord). Much like LiL, David Lynch stuff has a lot of theorycrafters and dumb dumb tables, and the leading theory for Rabbits is that its about God godlike entities mimicking what an average human life would be like, all inside a fictional setting. It also takes place within another one of his movies, but thats a deeper rabbit hole, pun intended.

Lastly is Eraserhead, and probably the most relevant of the bunch to Lessons In Love, as it's about an inexperienced single father who is failing at being a dad to his very deformed and kinda creepy baby. It's a horror-esque film dealing with the anxieties of being a father and ends with him, upon truly learning how deformed the kid actually is, kills the baby and possibly himself. Lots of religion and spiritual stuff embedded in this one.

posts.content_html_raw:
Okay, now that I'm actually rested and a bit more sane (relatively speaking), further theorizing on the next update. Option 1 (sex with Yumi with a monkey's paw) and Option 2 (we find out the content in the letter Nodoka wrote to herself/we find out what was buried beneath our feet) are still on the table.

Actual Option 3: Chinami dies. Her illness is set up early in Chapter 1, we had some foreshadowing in chapter 3 with a muffled cough within her dog mask, and the turnaround time between a foreshadow and the event playing out is about one year (Maya foreshadowed her own reset at the end of chapter 2, poofed at the end of chapter 3). This would absolutely break multiple characters beyond just Chika and Yumi, as she's become very close to the Tsukiokas. Her illness is also a Chekov's gun that becomes increasingly wasted if it ISN'T brought up in a narrative-relevant way for too long. So her dyiing -- and appearing to stay dead for at least one cycle before returning -- needs to happen eventually. Or perhaps she dies and becomes Something Different (tm), as the game has shown that death is sometimes merely a transition (Sekai).

That fact that "Chinami is likely to die" in a world where death within the narrative is portrayed as temporary (Bluejay) is an odd intersection, and at some point we need to find out exactly what that looks like.

Finally -- in her first appearance, Sensei calls her an angel -- a word that has become inreasingly loaded as the story's progressed.

I think this is the most likely option, honestly. Plus, this is a narrative opportunity to pile on Chika's misery, which is a thing this game loves to do.

Option 1 (sex with Yumi with a monkey's paw) and Option 2 (we find out the content in the letter Nodoka wrote to herself/we find out what was buried beneath our feet) are still on the table.
Actual Option 3: Chinami dies.  Her illness is set up early in Chapter 1, we had some foreshadowing in chapter 3 with a muffled cough within her dog mask, and the turnaround time between a foreshadow and the event playing out is about one year (Maya foreshadowed her own reset at the end of chapter 2, poofed at the end of chapter 3).  This would absolutely break multiple characters beyond just Chika and Yumi, as she's become very close to the Tsukiokas.  Her illness is also a Chekov's gun that becomes increasingly wasted if it ISN'T brought up in a narrative-relevant way for too long. I think this is the most likely option, honestly.  Plus, this is a narrative opportunity to pile on Chika's misery, which is a thing this game loves to do.

Actually, I've been thinking about that specific instance of AmIOkay saying "imagine the look on Maya's face when she finally slips" and, now that we know what slip means, that can actually confirm that Maya's alive.

Either she wasn't factory reset, or the factory reset itself means a different thing. Recall that when she was gone, she popped as an egg = she shifted somewhere else. What we can interpret is that, rather than being gone, Maya Prime was gone somewhere else (to the replica of heaven).

Additionally, who else is with her waiting at the place she slips to? AmIOkay! To see her face when she slips.

It's possible this has happened to Maya alone, or that it happens to everyone (see other Futaba stuck on that other plane). Maybe factory resetting doesn't erase anything, but rather transports the individual to another plane while installing a backup on Kumon-mi. This would also make sense with the fact that NAO can recall everything using the Wishing Well, well, she can do it because nothing was erased in the first place.

Basically, Maya can definitely be saved as she simply slipped somewhere, and maybe everyone can too.

Edit: aramaug has pointed out it's not AmIOkay that says the slip thing, but Long Maya. So keep that in mind.

Talking about the supposed big thing Selebus was planning since year one...I honestly don't know how much it narrows it down.

the last update of 2020 (he started on march of that year) was 0.11, which was the first Christmas update and the start of chapter 2. It ended with the other school crumbling so the big plan could include second floors students even if they weren't introduced to the game yet (except for Tsuneyo, Kirin, and Molly)

As for side characters, Yuki, Niki, Wakana, Osako, Tsubasa, and Tsukasa weren't introduced until chapter 2, Rika, Imani, and Nao-chan only made their first appearance on chapter 3

The last happy event introduced in year one was [Baby Finches] in v0.11, with there being a big gap until v0.18 part 2 introducing [Something Everyone Knows and Ignores]

Hopefully that helps us narrow it down as much as possible. What can really throw off the timeline I have been setting up is the big revamp he did from v0.1 to v0.6, but that still leaves us with the v0.7 to v0.11 as a constant in the timeline

If it has to do with any specific character, who is the one with the most potential to have some sort of reveal or event? it has to be something special considering it took the game years until Selebus felt now it is the suitable moment. At the very least, the event has to be almost to the level of Prime Maya going poof

Is it of emotional value? or of lore/story value? Will a character be perma killed and not reseted like Maya? Is it something to do with the Gods?

I don't know if we can narrow it down further by taking into consideration the character events next update, since most of them have other adjacent characters that could potentially make an apperance, but at least we can probably cross out: Osako, Wakana, Tsubasa, and Yuki

I don't think it has anything sexual to do with Chinami, back then Selebus had a hard stance against wizard stuff because he didn't want to get banned from patreon

There is a probability Chinami might die. Maybe the Gods or whoever is in control doesn't consider as important as the main cast and won't bother resurrecting her like with Makoto, or maybe if she dies of natural causes, it is something that can't be reseted

I mean there is the whole setup with Chika and Yumi, but it was something just recently introduced and I'm sure Selebus has been planning it for some time, but I don't think it is as important or major as Maya going poof.

Maybe it has something to do with her mother, but I don't remember much about her to have my own speculations

Same as with Chika. Or maybe we will get hints that give credence to the {Yumi & Sensei were lovers} theory. I mean there is this whole revelation Nodoka gave on this update about his blackouts


And he always experiences the most blackouts with Yumi. Hell one of his first ones was when he raped Yumi's mouth by the bridge, although that might have been less to do with Yumi and more to do with his sealed memories of Sekai doing the same to him as we saw in [Mother's Milk]

In fact I think that was what it was about,

I went to check just in case and is the literal same place and position lol so maybe it also has nothing to do with Yumi

Honestly I don't know what it could be about except something to do with Sara's past or Sana's brother. Maybe the theory of {Nozomu was Sara's professor and Sana's father} will finally bear fruit.

No idea. Tsubasa and Touka didn't have any events until v0.16 but Selebus probably already had the concept idea for them. Still I don't think it has something to do with them

More reveal about her parents? At that point in time we already had the Nightvision breakdown at the storage, and her breakdown during the thunderstorm when USER2 connects to Sensei

I mean we already know how her parents died, which was the biggest mistery of Miku's past back in the day. I also don't think it is as much of important story-wise

Maybe Sensei and Karin will have another conversation about what happened, but still, there is nothing related to Karin worth years of build up. Maybe she will find more information Ami's mother from her dad, talk to Sensei about it, and trigger another one of his episodes? but I think that might be a bit out of place.

I can't imagine anything significant happening with Makoto, unless it has something to do with Bluejay but dunno

So what I have learned from writing all of this. Is that I have learned nothing. lol I ain't confident on any of my assumptions, it has been years since I last played chapter 1 of the game, I only played the very beginning again but because of the revamp long ago.

1. Sensei being reset like Maya (unlikely)

2. One character being perma killed or becoming stuck in the TSS

3. Something to do with the outside world or the space war

4. More info about the upside down house

5. Nozomu's connection to the Sakakibaras

6. More reveal about the link between Nothing is Beautiful and Lessons in Love

7. A somewhat responsible adult side character (Wakana, Osako, Sara, Yuki) find concrete proof of Sensei having sexual relationship with his students. I don't include Tsubasa in the list since she is insane.

8. Chika and Yumi have a complete breakup of their friendship. Even if it isn't really a situation of plot importance, that will still change the dynamics between characters. In fact it could potential spark into bigger conflicts between the students, each starting to create even more separate cliches.
FACTIONS, ALLIES AND FOES. CAT FIGHTS. DORM WARS WITH REAL CONSEQUENCES
WAR WAR WAR WAR BLOOD BLOOD BLOOD BLOOD STEEL STEEL STEEL STEEL

In any case, I hope we got more clues with future previews images & event names

spoilers.title: Timeline
spoilers.html:
the last update of 2020 (he started on march of that year) was 0.11, which was the first Christmas update and the start of chapter 2. It ended with the other school crumbling so the big plan could include second floors students even if they weren't introduced to the game yet (except for Tsuneyo, Kirin, and Molly)

As for side characters, Yuki, Niki, Wakana, Osako, Tsubasa, and Tsukasa weren't introduced until chapter 2, Rika, Imani, and Nao-chan only made their first appearance on chapter 3

The last happy event introduced in year one was [Baby Finches] in v0.11, with there being a big gap until v0.18 part 2 introducing [Something Everyone Knows and Ignores]

Hopefully that helps us narrow it down as much as possible. What can really throw off the timeline I have been setting up is the big revamp he did from v0.1 to v0.6, but that still leaves us with the v0.7 to v0.11 as a constant in the timeline

Sara's coping mechanism after losing her son was to try as hard as possible to pretend like he never even existed, so any pictures would have been put away ages ago.

Perhaps by… suffering some kind of tremendous loss, a ‘complete’ person’s life is suddenly now ‘incomplete’?

Taking a look at the current (and past) RAS members as examples:

Sensei - Where to start? He’s lost a lot. Sekai. His brother. His parents. His innocence. Not to mention, like Yuu, he’s special; a wildcard.

Maya - Maya Prime lost Akira, the love of her life, making her incomplete. She then made a divine wish that she could be with him forever, and like the story of Altair and Vega, was delivered to her in the worst way imaginable, leading to her curse and most likely the time loops themselves.

Ayane - She got pregnant with Himawari before Reset 3, somehow got the idea to meet with Sensei on the roof, and then showed up during said reset. Once the reset itself happened, Ayane was gone, along with the unborn Himawari. Her baby was now lost, making Ayane incomplete. Come Reset 4, Ayane shows up on the roof again, and this time, doesn’t disappear.

Makoto - Makoto started becoming aware of the time fuckery around the time of the solo beach trip with her, Sensei and Miku, but didn’t really begin perceiving things until after the death of her father. Masahiro was her reason for pushing herself in school and making her the person she was. She wanted to make him proud. And now that he’s gone, Makoto is now an incomplete person. In Reset 6, she shows up on the roof.

I could be a bit off, but it seems plausible.

What triggers someone to begin being able to perceive their past selves memories? You all know i'm too dumb to get this shit on my own so what do you guys make of this? DeSkelly? Mooney? Fdsas? Maug?
Click to expand...
Honestly, I think it kind of comes down to this:
Reina - "Are you happy here?"
(Nothing is Beautiful)

Maya - "Are you happy here?"
(Chapter 1 'Normal Office Visit' Main Event)

Ami - "Are you happy here, Sensei?"
(Chapter 1 Ami 'No One Can See Us' Event)

Special Ami/HOPE(?) - "ARE YOU HAPPY HERE???"
(Chapter 3 'Memories' Main Event)

Being Whole may just translate to being Happy. Most of these girls are "happy" with how things are, even if it's not perfect. They are happy with their script that they were given. Happy to play the girl they are scripted to play.

When they truly go off script is when they become aware. When things happen that change who they are and what they want, or when they are not "happy here", they seem to become aware. Sana, for example, is wanting to be Happy, now:
Sana - "I think I just want to be happy."
- "And I'm not sure if I've ever really felt that way before."
(Chapter 4 Sana 'Taller' Event)
Which seems to have made it so that she can acknowledge the reality of the world. She's not the same character she was scripted to be. She just didn't care about the weird things going on, until Sensei mentioned it.
  • Ayane had been happy until she got knocked up, and then lost the baby, which she still remembers. She wanted to be a mother, and that's what made her happy, what kept her going, but this world wouldn't allow that. She's had to go off script to be happy ever since.
  • Makoto has had to change again and again since Bluejay to be Happy. Bluejay broke her, then she was reset, but the memories of Bluejay forced her to try to change, then her father's death nearly broke her, but Ami helped her (Ami's the caretaker and cared for both Ayane and Makoto before they became aware), which allowed Makoto to instead focus on what makes her Happy. This is when the Unbluejay happens, she tricks Sensei into signing marriage papers, and then she's shown to have become aware of things. Her trying to be Happy, instead of simply being "happy here", may have been why.
  • Yumi was forced to re-evaluate what makes her Happy after Nodoka forced her to face herself, Chika, and what her future might look like (Yuki). This led to her trying to be Happy, by letting Yuki back in, being nice to Noriko and Futaba, etc.
  • Tsuneyo is a little different, but assuming that what happened to Molly forced her to re-evaluate what makes her Happy, then Sensei taking her on that date also changed what she thinks will make her Happy (Sensei), then this may explain why she's become aware.
Nodoka seems to be trying to liberate everyone, presumably like her mother tried to, in the past, from the script. From the game. She's doing this by more or less:
Nodoka - "And the best way to for me to create a world worth living in is to mutilate the one we have beyond recognition."
(Chapter 4 Makoto 'The Pit of Despair' Event)

However, trying to break the mold seems to have crippled Nodoka's mother mentally, and may do the same to Nodoka. Kyoko didn't seem to have a Sensei to help like Nodoka might, though:
Nodoka - "Everything we do, and everything we think is not the result of conscious thought, but a predetermined script that we're simply-"
- "I can't...end up like her! I can't! I won't! I...NGAAAAH! FUCK YOU, BRAIN! FUCK YOU, GOD! YOU CANT...HIDE...FOREVER!!!!"
- "A...Akira! You know too! I...can tell! You know...I'm not insane! But she...she never had that! She never had...someone like you!"
- "Everything...I do...NGAAAAAH! It's all...to break the mold!...To liberate us!"
(Chapter 4 Nodoka 'Mille Crepe' Event)
For those unaware, Nodoka's mother isn't able to take care of herself:
Futaba - "Nodoka is constantly moving back and forth between the dorms and her home because her mom isn't..."
- "Well, she isn't really able to function on her own. But that's really all I feel comfortable telling you..."
(Chapter 3 Futaba 'This Infected Wound' Event)
And we presumably know why, now. She fought the world, alone, and...lost.

Although, like Nao has pointed out:
Nao - "There can be no coincidences when the human idea of free will is writing one's own script when it is something more powerful than you scripting your scriptwriting in the first place."
(Chapter 3 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event)
I'm not sure if Nodoka's attempt at liberation is because she's actually smart enough to escape her script, or if it's simply how she was scripted.

Her noticing the stain, and her notes, may simply be what's supposed to happen, but if so, then who's to say that becoming aware, or getting to the roof during a reset, isn't part of the script.

We know it technically is, but if Sel is going that route, then this really can only end rather depressingly.

Edit: Also Maya and Sensei may have become aware because without eachother they weren't "happy here".

Yumi was forced to re-evaluate what makes her Happy after Nodoka forced her to face herself, Chika, and what her future might look like (Yuki). This led to her trying to be Happy, by letting Yuki back in, being nice to Noriko and Futaba, etc.
Tsuneyo is a little different, but assuming that what happened to Molly forced her to re-evaluate what makes her Happy, then Sensei taking her on that date also changed what she thinks will make her Happy (Sensei), then this may explain why she's become aware.
Nodoka seems to be trying to liberate everyone, presumably like her mother tried to, in the past, from the script. From the game. She's doing this by more or less:
Spoiler
Nodoka - "And the best way to for me to create a world worth living in is to mutilate the one we have beyond recognition."
(Chapter 4 Makoto 'The Pit of Despair' Event)
However, trying to break the mold seems to have crippled Nodoka's mother mentally, and may do the same to Nodoka. Kyoko didn't seem to have a Sensei to help like Nodoka might, though:
Spoiler
Nodoka - "Everything we do, and everything we think is not the result of conscious thought, but a predetermined script that we're simply-"
- "I can't...end up like her! I can't! I won't! I...NGAAAAH! FUCK YOU, BRAIN! FUCK YOU, GOD! YOU CANT...HIDE...FOREVER!!!!"
- "A...Akira! You know too! I...can tell! You know...I'm not insane! But she...she never had that! She never had...someone like you!"
- "Everything...I do...NGAAAAAH! It's all...to break the mold!...To liberate us!"
(Chapter 4 Nodoka 'Mille Crepe' Event)
For those unaware, Nodoka's mother isn't able to take care of herself:
Spoiler
Futaba - "Nodoka is constantly moving back and forth between the dorms and her home because her mom isn't..."
- "Well, she isn't really able to function on her own. But that's really all I feel comfortable telling you..."
(Chapter 3 Futaba 'This Infected Wound' Event)
And we presumably know why, now. She fought the world, alone, and...
lost
.
Although, like Nao has pointed out:
Spoiler
Nao - "There can be no coincidences when the human idea of free will is writing one's own script when it is something more powerful than you scripting your scriptwriting in the first place."
(Chapter 3 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event)
I'm not sure if Nodoka's attempt at liberation is because she's actually smart enough to escape her script, or if it's simply
how
she was scripted.
Her noticing the stain, and her notes, may simply be what's supposed to happen, but if so, then who's to say that becoming aware, or getting to the roof during a reset, isn't part of the script.
We know it
technically
is, but if Sel is going that route, then this really can only end rather depressingly.
Edit: Also Maya and Sensei may have become aware because without eachother they weren't "happy here".

A longer post on Nodoka is on my to-do list, but my basic understanding of what's going on with her is that she's able to receive fragmentary thoughts and memories from one or more "other Nodokas", probably past versions of her that were factory reset. In contrast, the other characters also have these other selves, but they aren't mentally connected to them in any way.

If I understand correctly, what she believes is that:
  • Each time (for example) Futaba is factory reset, she's replaced with an exact copy of her pre-reset version. When presented with the same situations, she will act in exactly the same way - like an actor playing the same character each time. She's whole in the sense that the current Futaba is always a single consciousness in a single body.
  • Each time Nodoka is factory reset, a new piece is added to a connected web of Nodoka conscioussnesses. Since she can (to some extent) draw on her past experiences, she's able to act differently than she has in previous cycles. On the other hand, she's not whole because the "real Nodoka" is spread among all these different pieces.
It's definitely possible that this is connected in some way to being able to comprehend the cycles, but I'm still not sure what the trigger is. For Nodoka it seems to be a hereditary thing, she's said her mother had the same thing and it drove her insane (and her father is probably Yuu, who also had visions).

Click to expand...
Hmm, I don't think it would add something very substantial for RAS business because it lacks comparable examples. To explain this I want to point out what Nodoka currently could grasp first because I feel like we're trying to tackle more than one question all at once:
  1. Individuals can pass between planes. Types of passing vary. Two types that are validated by Nodoka in this update are physical teleportation and entering a mental state where actions of your body are guided by memories.
  2. The source of aforementioned memories isn't limited to "the you in this plane". You can be guided by memories that are, in this context, from "the you(s) in other plane(s)".
  3. Unlike the rest of the girls that would just "A-anyway!", Nodoka utilizes this phenomenon to guide herself, and ultimately finds out that the world is repeating. Thus her extension to this conclusion is that a script must have existed in order for a world to indefinitely repeat itself.
By listing these, my expanded bullet points are:
  • How Nodoka gains herself awareness to the fuckery is not simply from perceiving her past selves, but from experimenting with them and somehow answering the big question. The importance of "being whole or not" in this matter or in her case is not addressed.
  • Besides, I can't tell whether "no longer being whole" is the cause or the effect here. Nodoka can be referring to a mental state that is traumatized, or a mental state that is a superposition of selves from multiple planes combined.
  • Even if "no longer being whole" is the key to perceiving past selves memories, being able to perceive doesn't necessarily equate a trip to the rooftop (Ayane in reset3 with zero awareness), or landing you a place in RAS (Yumi and Tsuneyo in reset5), or timely landing you a place in RAS (Makoto remembered things way before reset6). Therefore trying to find what's not whole about the potential RAS members to correlate their fuckery awareness feels less like writing an answer to a question but more like writing a question for an answer.
A little sidetrack here is that one might even argue the definition of "past selves memories". Loose definition is any memory that doesn't make chronological sense, while stringent definition will be the memories from selves in the past cycles. Currently only Yumi is shown to be qualified under the stringent definition as someone who can apparently remember the detentions other iterations gave her. Still, remembering that hasn't landed her a place in RAS yet.

Considering you two, I guess Maya got resetted because she finally found happiness with Akira. She realized he remembered a lot of stuff and still loved her. But, paradoxically, that's what killed her – her own happiness. You shouldn't really be happy in this world.
Click to expand...
Maya Prime also seemed to have her memories be erased until there was only Akira:
Spoiler
Maya - "I've already...given up everything else..."
- "All that's left...are the memories of you!..."
(Chapter 3 'Remember to Smile' Main Event)
So, there's literally nothing besides Sensei that
could
have made her happy at the end.
fdsasdf_p said:
A little sidetrack here is that one might even argue the definition of "past selves memories". Loose definition is
any memory that doesn't make chronological sense
, while stringent definition will be
the memories from selves in the past cycles
. Currently only Yumi is shown to be qualified under the stringent definition as someone who can apparently remember the detentions other iterations gave her. Still, remembering that hasn't landed her a place in RAS yet.
Click to expand...
Technically, Yumi might just be remembering what happened before the resets:
Spoiler
Yumi - "You think I just up and forgot about all those fucking creepy ass detentions?! Get real!"
(Chapter 1 Yumi 'Five Million Dollars' Event)
Yumi - "Then...example. You ain't ever given me detention...right?"
Sensei - "No. Too much work."
Yumi - "Yeah, exactly. Then why the fuck do I have so many memories of you doin' that? And why the fuck are they all so goddamn illegal and rapey and shit?"
Sensei - "If I am, it's unintentional. Hell, maybe I even did that shit to you in
this
universe but have no recollection of it because my mind's gotten all tangled up in the threads of time."
(Chapter 4 Yumi 'Wake Me Up When It's  Over' Event)
Or maybe even during the Beachmas timeskip since Sensei and Yumi were hanging out a lot during it apparently:
Spoiler
Chika - "This isn't what you wanted to talk to Sensei about tonight, is it? Because I was assuming it was something a little more...I don't know, important?"
Yumi - "Important how?"
Chika - "Beats me. Maybe something about how much time you guys have been spending together lately?"
Yumi - "We've...what? Why?
When?
"
(Chapter 3 'Shelter' Main Event)
Which may have been shown earlier in the 'Redeemer' Main Event:
Spoiler
Sensei - "A̶n̶d̶ ̶r̶u̶n̶ ̶a̶w̶a̶y̶ ̶w̶h̶i̶l̶e̶ ̶y̶o̶u̶ ̶s̶t̶i̶l̶l̶ ̶c̶a̶n̶.̶"
Yumi's memories have been a mess since she seemingly died in Reset 5, and since Beachmas, they have been questionable due to that 2 months timeskip.
Besides Maya Prime, only Tsuneyo and Sensei have seemed to recall memories from past timelines. Tsuneyo recalled Sensei saying something when she wasn't part of the class yet, and hearing about the Resets, while Sensei recalled a crying Maya (Prime?) jerking him off, to death, back during the first reset in this timeline.

aramaug said:
It might have been too strong to say that Yuu is "probably" her father, but there is circumstantial evidence:
  1. Kyoko is one of the residents of the upside down house along with Saki, two other Nothing is Beautiful characters, and an unnamed male. Because of the NiB connection, people think it's Yuu.
  2. In the event where Sensei trades nudes with Otoha, he suddenly gets weird thoughts apparently coming from Nodoka's father ("Can you hear this Kyoko? Your daughter is a nightmare. She has my eyes.") with the attached photograph on the screen, probably meant to be from the upside down house. It's more likely these come from someone Sensei has a connection with rather than a random unnamed character. View attachment 3900374
  3. There's joking references to Sensei and Nodoka being secret siblings which could be foreshadowing. See the "secret family" section of my post here.
Click to expand...
The timelines don't match though. Nodoka is Ami's age. The only possible way for Nodoka to be Akira's sister is if she time-travelled, she'd have to be Yuu's granddaughter if anything (which isn't likely because she's Kyoko's daughter).

Also, if Yuu was around to impregnate Kyoko by the time Ami was born, then Saki's trauma would make little sense. Why would she be so hard on Akira (for his similarity to Yuu) if Yuu was around and well enough to go around getting people pregnant?

Also, if Yuu was around and well, it'd make absolutely no sense for him not to care for Akira when he started showing the same symptoms as him. It's understandable that Saki'd react badly to it because it had already taken her husband. But for Yuu? He'd be well, and thus Akira's issues would be much less of a big deal since he was able to thrive even though he had them as well.

Pareidolia seems to be using her. We used to think it was HOPE, mainly because it seems HOPE was involved with Sara, and there's the theory Sana is the daughter of Nozomu himself. However, since that one event Pareidolia "saved" Sana/slipped her back to kumon-mi (or even engineered the whole situation), it seems he's intent on using her.

There are many instances (like spiders and rabbits), but, directly, Sana was the one in Akira's dream as spring arrived (Pareidolia's season), and he also predicted what would happen on the beach (maybe even was the one guiding Sana).

Indirectly, Sana has been involved with Sekai and/but Sekai's actual involvement with Pareidolia is up in the air (they're working "together" in stomachache, and she was the one guiding Akira right before he first fingered Sana).

Lastly, Himawari/her rogue team has actively rebelled against Pareidolia (this can be seen in "miserably ever after"), and the fact that narrator (most likely Himawari) tells Akira to stay in the room, and imediately after Sana comes to get him out of the room, would point out Pareidolia as the opposed party.

The gods are starting to gather pawns for the game that is starting.The current players are as follows.

1)Hope
2)Himawari and Co
3)Wires
4)Pareidolia and Sekai

For the sake of the argument im using the theory that everything thats happening is because the 3 MAIN gods of this universe(Pareidolia Wires Hope) have different goals and that creates conflict.

Pareidolia wishes for chaos and destruction.He wishes to destroy everything around Akira not because he wants to remake the world or anything like that.Pareidolia is just a very sadistic entity.

Hope wishes to reform the world.He wants to change the way things are and in order to do that he NEEDS Akira.He has developed an unhealthy obsession with him and he has even went as far as temporarely descending into our world(Which i will refer to it as TERMINAL 23) through Yasu.

Wires is the closest thing Akira has to an ally in this game.Wires has helped him stay sane from the very beginning,he has tried to stop Akira from making irreversible mistakes but to no avail.He wants to maintain order but he is either weakened or is just in general not on par with the other 2.

One potential theory that ive been letting stew goes as follows.

We have 4 seasons in kumon-mi.Winter Summer Spring and Autumn.

Now we know that Spring is Pareidolias season but we cant exactly be sure about all the other seasons.But for the sake of it lets suppose it goes as follows.

Spring~Pareidolia
Summer~Hope
Automn~Wires
Winter~Nao(Im supposing Nao is the god that Maya prayed to to reset the world)

My theory goes as follows.Each god represents one season in kumon-mi so the corresponding god is stronger in their season.They are able to interfere with the world around them and do a lot more weird god stuff.Now i believe that Pareidolias "Endless Spring" is him artifically keeping this up as his first move towards his goal.

If we follow that theory then Pareidolia already has 2 wonderful pawns.Sekai and now potentially Sana(As Moonflare said i also believe that Adult Sana appearing in Senseis dream was Pareidolias attempt to influence him).

Hope has Yasu and his angels.

Wires has Tsuneyo and her father.

Nao is still a mystery.

But yea TLDR:I believe that we are in the beginning of a game of chess between gods to decide the future of this world.We arent an active player,we are the most valuable piece.

View attachment 3900059 View attachment 3900060 Sana - "I think I just want to be happy."
- "And I'm not sure if I've ever really felt that way before."
(Chapter 4 Sana 'Taller' Event)
Which seems to have made it so that she can acknowledge the reality of the world. She's not the same character she was scripted to be. She just didn't care about the weird things going on, until Sensei mentioned it.
  • Ayane had been happy until she got knocked up, and then lost the baby, which she still remembers. She wanted to be a mother, and that's what made her happy, what kept her going, but this world wouldn't allow that. She's had to go off script to be happy ever since.
  • Makoto has had to change again and again since Bluejay to be Happy. Bluejay broke her, then she was reset, but the memories of Bluejay forced her to try to change, then her father's death nearly broke her, but Ami helped her (Ami's the caretaker and cared for both Ayane and Makoto before they became aware), which allowed Makoto to instead focus on what makes her Happy. This is when the Unbluejay happens, she tricks Sensei into signing marriage papers, and then she's shown to have become aware of things. Her trying to be Happy, instead of simply being "happy here", may have been why.
  • Yumi was forced to re-evaluate what makes her Happy after Nodoka forced her to face herself, Chika, and what her future might look like (Yuki). This led to her trying to be Happy, by letting Yuki back in, being nice to Noriko and Futaba, etc.
  • Tsuneyo is a little different, but assuming that what happened to Molly forced her to re-evaluate what makes her Happy, then Sensei taking her on that date also changed what she thinks will make her Happy (Sensei), then this may explain why she's become aware.

View attachment 3900264 Nodoka - "And the best way to for me to create a world worth living in is to mutilate the one we have beyond recognition."
(Chapter 4 Makoto 'The Pit of Despair' Event)

View attachment 3900194 View attachment 3900196 View attachment 3900197 View attachment 3900198 Nodoka - "Everything we do, and everything we think is not the result of conscious thought, but a predetermined script that we're simply-"
- "I can't...end up like her! I can't! I won't! I...NGAAAAH! FUCK YOU, BRAIN! FUCK YOU, GOD! YOU CANT...HIDE...FOREVER!!!!"
- "A...Akira! You know too! I...can tell! You know...I'm not insane! But she...she never had that! She never had...someone like you!"
- "Everything...I do...NGAAAAAH! It's all...to break the mold!...To liberate us!"
(Chapter 4 Nodoka 'Mille Crepe' Event)
For those unaware, Nodoka's mother isn't able to take care of herself:
View attachment 3900202 View attachment 3900203 Futaba - "Nodoka is constantly moving back and forth between the dorms and her home because her mom isn't..."
- "Well, she isn't really able to function on her own. But that's really all I feel comfortable telling you..."
(Chapter 3 Futaba 'This Infected Wound' Event)
And we presumably know why, now. She fought the world, alone, and...lost.

Although, like Nao has pointed out:
View attachment 3900160 Nao - "There can be no coincidences when the human idea of free will is writing one's own script when it is something more powerful than you scripting your scriptwriting in the first place."
(Chapter 3 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event)

RE: Nodoka and breaking the script —
I mean, that's the issue philosophers have been struggling with since at least the Middle Ages, right? Free will vs. predistination. Are you making X choice because you want to, or because the Prime Mover/Creator/Universe made you? Are you actually a free agent, or simply a billiard ball with delusions of grandeur. And there's no way to resolve that question, though at least modern physics gives us some wiggle room.

The Asian religions largely deal with this problem by viewing this life as simply a step in your soul's longer journey. The choices you make and actions you take (or don't take) — your karma/gō — relative to your predestined fate — your dharma/daruma — weigh you down or lift you up as you pass from one life to the following one so that, next time around, you come back as an ant or a god. Or, more likely, something in between.

Which, now that I think about it, might have a certain bearing on the Isekai and Denpa genres, and especially a game world that's constantly being reset in endless time loops. Hmm.

Maybe Maya Prime wasn't erased, but finally achieved Nirvana?

(Though if that is MP in "Heaven," a) she sure doesn't seem happy let alone blissful, and b) she's still herself, which, if she'd actually achieved release from the round of sorrows, she wouldn't be — she'd be dissolved into the Buddha Mind that is the universe. Eesh.)

That said, Sel seems to have a much more Western view of all the moral/religious/philosophical BS. I mean, Yasu's church, the presence and actions of the various gods... It all feels more influenced by Christianity and Greek myths than by Hinduism or Buddhism.

ETA: And of course, there's a certain irony to exploring the idea of free will... in a scripted game. Heh.

ETA2: The cycles of abuse victims becoming abusers in this game seems to suggest its own kind of predestination/scripting.

That said, after reading Comiies's interesting rundown, it occurs to me that
each of the three "C" gods corresponds roughly to one of the major deities in Hinduism (who are also recognized in Buddhism):
  1. Vishnu the Creator/Dreamer = Hope (Yasu's god)
  2. Brahma the Maintainer = Wires (Tsuneyo's god?)
  3. Shiva the Destroyer = Pareidolia (who seems to be connected to Sekai and some of the other agents of chaos — don't touch my Sana!)
In that view, perhaps Nao (Maya's and Nao-chan's god, maybe?) would be ... Maya. Who, depending on which version of the myths you're looking at is either the universe itself or the illusion that is our perception of the universe. Or maybe Kali, black time, who is the mother and devourer of all.

spoilers.html:
each of the three "C" gods corresponds roughly to one of the major deities in Hinduism (who are also recognized in Buddhism):
  1. Vishnu the Creator/Dreamer = Hope (Yasu's god)
  2. Brahma the Maintainer = Wires (Tsuneyo's god?)
  3. Shiva the Destroyer = Pareidolia (who seems to be connected to Sekai and some of the other agents of chaos — don't touch my Sana!)
In that view, perhaps Nao (Maya's and Nao-chan's god, maybe?) would be ... Maya. Who, depending on which version of the myths you're looking at is either the universe itself or the illusion that is our perception of the universe. Or maybe Kali, black time, who is the mother and devourer of all.

posts.content_html_raw:
Some other questions/thoughts about what Nodoka is letting on in this update.

Q1: What does Nodoka mean when she reaffirmed that Futaba is special? Who is this she?

The she here is highly likely to be Kyoko; the groceries, the attic, and the fact that she's now a proven special case.
I just fail to see how that makes Futaba special; or maybe I misunderstood what Nodoka means here. She perhaps isn't alluding to the origin that makes Futaba special, but is simply saying that a certain she also went through similar paranormal events and is thus deemed special by Nodoka, and now Futaba qualifies as well.

Q2: Can the when and where Nodoka recovered the note her other selves wrote for herself be confirmed by an event?

I wanted to guess that "a place that God himself could never find" is that abandoned school featured in Beyond the Reach of God, but the date couldn't be correct. That event took place in early Ch3 and before Halloween wars so it's for sure not December. However, the rest of that event seems very fitting; venturing out to find something, a mark that resembles lower case T on the ground (perhaps the exact same spot where amiokay got crucified on the cross in The Letter 'T'), the event name itself, etc.

Another possible place is the Wishing Well / The Library where Nodoka is submerged in the pool, but this is supported merely by thoughts like "why not".

Or, since Nodoka from time to time went apeshit well before Beyond the Reach of God, so she might've located this note a lot earlier behind the scene and has been trying to crack it for some time, though in those scenarios she could very well be studying Kyoko's words and not her own. In addition, my impression is that Nodoka would know what her own note meant as soon as she retrieved it; she just struggled with the mechanisms until Yasu enlightened her. All in all, it’s relatively possible that the note was retrieved BTS but it feels a lot less enticing if that’s the case.

The timelines don't match though. Nodoka is Ami's age. The only possible way for Nodoka to be Akira's sister is if she time-travelled, she'd have to be Yuu's granddaughter if anything (which isn't likely because she's Kyoko's daughter).

Also, if Yuu was around to impregnate Kyoko by the time Ami was born, then Saki's trauma would make little sense. Why would she be so hard on Akira (for his similarity to Yuu) if Yuu was around and well enough to go around getting people pregnant?

Also, if Yuu was around and well, it'd make absolutely no sense for him not to care for Akira when he started showing the same symptoms as him. It's understandable that Saki'd react badly to it because it had already taken her husband. But for Yuu? He'd be well, and thus Akira's issues would be much less of a big deal since he was able to thrive even though he had them as well.
Click to expand...
I'm going off of memory here so correct me if I'm wrong, but I think our only evidence for Yuu's absence is what we're told in "Goodnight Moon" (which might not even be accurate, it seems to be narrated by Pareidolia). In any case we're not told that Yuu was dead (or how or when he died), so any of the following are possible:
  • Rather than dying, Yuu abandoned his family with Saki.
  • Memories involving Yuu were retroactively altered, hence why Pareidolia says that no one remembers him.
  • The Kyoko in the upside down house was impregnated and this somehow made the Kyoko in Kumon-mi pregnant.
  • Kyoko physically traveled to a different plane (like Futaba in TSS2) and was impregnated there.
I'm not saying that any of these are likely, I just want to point out there's too much that we don't know. I find it easier to accept that supernatural fuckery allows Yuu to be Nodoka's father than that the other clues are red herrings.

(Far as I know) Surnames are, at least generally/historically, written with the same kanji and not changed. It'd be like adding a silent h or a to an English last name randomly, but weirder. The kanji can change the meaning or etymology, though. You can have two words that are homophones but different spelling in English, or spelling/kanji in sushi-language. That's what makes it extra difficult.

After looking into it a little bit, most of the names I double checked are well-known locations/cities, surnames (that often double as or originate from locations, i.e. toponymic names,) or the names of well-known people/characters/things. So I think Selebus most likely racked his brain for or googled common names and things to use for the characters that fit the matching initials thing. That's also the simplest explanation. I don't believe he knows any Japanese, but who knows.

If someone more proficient in Japanese recognizes additional meanings / spellings / origins for names that seem plausible, there might be something for a couple of characters. I have one vague possibility in mind, but that's a huge stretch. I'm not qualified to posit anything.

fdsasdf_p said:
That's quite a lot of extrapolation solely based off the fact that Futaba uses lavender-scented perfume. There are so many assumptions here that need to be all correct in order to have "Yuko aka DOUBT being this she" make sense when we can't even confidently discern what the upside down house really is.

To streamline your claim (apologies if I sound impolitely sarcastic), that means Yuko can leave the upside down house for books and groceries thus can also travel through planes, and got pregnant on aisle 23 when she was outside, and gave birth to Futaba, and had her adopted by others without Futaba's knowing it, and Futaba chose lavender-scented perfume because of the hair of a woman who Futaba doesn't know that's her bio-mom, and definitely not because it simply smells good.

I get that you're trying to fill the blank between "Futaba traveled through planes for the first time" and "There is someone in the upside down that has lavender for hair and Futaba actually uses lavender-scented perfume" and explore a potential bridge, but to do so all of the things described above would have to be true to a certain extent, otherwise the chance of this she being Yuko drops enormously.
Click to expand...
You're getting my point backwards. I'm not starting from the idea that Nodoka is talking about Futaba's mother and then extrapolating that it must be Yuko, I'm starting from the idea that Nodoka is talking about Yuko and that Yuko and Futaba have been connected before, and then trying to interpret what Nodoka says about that connection here.

The things that Nodoka says about "she" in that passage point to Yuko more than they do to Kyoko:
  • "She" has the key to the attic. In "Lavender", Kyoko keeps telling Yuko to come downstairs while the screen shows stairs and "there's something in the attic" repeated.
  • "She" is the one who gets the groceries. Yuko is the one who fills the shelves with new books (so she has the ability to get physical items), and right after Kyoko tells her to "repopulate the shelves", her next sentence is telling her to put food on the table. When searching for something else, I just ran across an image from an old Apollo259 post that shows a shopping list with books and groceries signed with a Y.
Not to mention that Yuko is clearly special in some way since Pareidolia doesn't list her as one of the five named residents of the house.

At no point did I suggest that Futaba wears lavender perfume because of a conscious memory of Yuko's hair. Supernatural/symbolic parallels are very much a part of this game.

But in any case, the connection between Futaba, lavender, and the upside down house is more than just her perfume. When Sensei tries to remember her story of the upside down house, he hallucinates (thanks to Pareidolia?) lavender plants over her.

In her first sexual scene, he compares her to a lavender garden.
When Nodoka brings up the girl with lavender hair, Sensei explicitly connects her to Futaba.
There's probably more that I don't remember. Honestly I didn't think it was controversial that there is some connection between Futaba and the girl with the lavender hair. Do you think Selebus intends it to be coincidence that two different characters are so strongly associated with lavender imagery?

It doesn't have to mean anything, but Nodoka's interest in Futaba seems to parallel Kyoko's obsession with Yuko.
I forget the event(s), but at some point Nodoka implied that she only became friends with Futaba in the first place (which was pre-resets) because there was something unusually interesting about her.

The mother possibility was just speculation based purely on the way that Nodoka worded her sentence, it was not an idea I seriously considered before this update. To me, Nodoka saying "you're special because she was" implies more than just similarity, she thinks that there is causation involved. Heredity is just one possible cause.

After thinking about it more, it's unlikely that Yuko is her mother. At some point Futaba said she looks like her mother, which probably means that she isn't adopted and her mother doesn't have lavender hair.

Gotcha, I was mainly fixated on how to create a scenario where Yuko could be fitted as Futaba's real mom and I couldn't do it.

And quite frankly, I was struggling with the said 'connection' between Yuko and Futaba quite a lot if the sole shared element is just lavender. For example, I could say the reason for the lavender imagery in Sensei's vision or him explicitly 'connecting' to Futaba when the girl with lavender hair was mentioned is simply because Futaba wears lavender-scented perfume; that's just how she smells like and thus that's what he thinks of when his mind wanders or prompted (especially in the latter example Sensei even told you why he thought of Futaba amidst of Nodoka's rambling). It's not Futaba reminding him of lavender or lavender reminding him of Futaba out of nowhere.

What I'm getting at is that Futaba left this flowery impression on Sensei all by herself via her own choice of perfume. That's why lavender imagery/the use of the word lavender/thinking about a girl with lavender hair colocalizes with Futaba so much in Sensei's head. As long as it can be explained by something mundane, I don't see the need to force an unexplainable connection here between Futaba and Yuko using lavender, as it feels just like an unnecessary false positive. Without other supporting evidence looking at Futaba/Yuko from other angles, we're left with believing Selly being intentional about the choice of using lavender to present these two characters, and that really isn't a solid lead. In addition, the inconsistency in Yuko's name is also not a valid argument in this matter; it just tells you that Yuko's role might be different from other residents but it cannot be linked back to Futaba.

The only thing I'd give a pass around lavender is, what you mentioned, the seemingly mirroring behaviors of Nagasawa females fancying other females with lavender elements, as this is showing the similar lesbo energy between Kyoko and Nodoka, but NOT proving the connection between Yuko and Futaba.

HOWEVER, I find the attic and the groceries bits quite interesting, and honestly a whole lot more convincing than the lavender bits. I was thinking whether those bits were extremely exclusive to Yuko (like, what are the odds of Kyoko or another person being the one that had the key and collected groceries as some form of rotating responsibilities?), but then I remembered that Nodoka supposedly can only know this via Kyoko's words, hence whoever Nodoka is referring to should have a very high chance to be the same person Kyoko mentioned about the attic and the grocery. The question now becomes "why Nodoka draws this comparison?" Is she just connecting them because of the superficial lavender elements, or is there actually something a lot more substantial deep down?

Christ, you're all fucking stupid. Morons. Buffoons, even. Yasu obviously deserves the most attention. All she's ever done is her best despite feeling like nothing. She's the toy of a false god, she has no one, and still devotes herself to what she's been told is what's right. She is an innocent little angel, deserving of freedom, love, care, and a place in the world. She deservers the chance and the dignity that comes with knowing what it's like for most people to be a little girl, someone's sister or daughter, someone's best friend, even a normal human being. A chance to grow and experience the little joys and comforts that come with people seeing you just as they see everyone else, for your best friend to not feel like your caretaker, for people to treat you with respect. When will she have done enough to deserve that much? When will she have done enough to deserve our respect? When will we see Yasu not as a traumatized girl, or a walking radio for some other-worldly person or being, but as a person?

Oh, and also, she has a machine gun. (Thanks Kittyhawk ♥)

Click to expand...
People are afraid for the wizards (and rightfully so) but most people look at this game in a different lens than I do.

There's a lot of players who abstain from following the green route because of obvious reasons, and I find it justifiable, but the green route by all means IS the best route AND the "canon" route.

I noticed that a thing has gone under many people's radar, the fact that ALL the USERS want you to follow the green path, despite having different end-goals, but why is that the case?

One could understand that pareidolia's motivation is just a sick desire to see everything defiled, thus destroying her, taking the plug, and so on, but what about the other two?

Fucking girls, in a sense, is a form of taking power, it's what WIRES tells you in his sanctuary audio very early into the game, you are taking their essence, and you need ALL of the essence which can only be attained through fucking every girl you come across, a stronger Akira is a benefit to all of the USERS, but for different reasons.

HOPE wants you to follow the green route so that he can become the most powerful and create a world in his image.
WIRES wants you to follow the green route so that he can rebuild the girls and maintain the world as it is.
Pareidolia wants you to follow the green route so that he can destroy everything as he desires.

Not following the green route means that you will be powerless when facing what's to come near the end.

You need to keep breaking them, taking their essence, and that includes the Wizards, but it will all be okay if you choose to repair them and follow the wires.

In a sick twisted way, doing the bad thing is not the bad thing at all if you look far into the distance.

Typically every 2 Resets, and every Chapter, there's a seasonal change.

Chapter 1 is in Summer. After Reset 2 (There is Nothing), it becomes Winter and Chapter 2. After Reset 4 (A Life of Prizes), it became Summer again and Chapter 3. After Reset 6 (Times New Roman), it became Spring, and Chapter 4.

Presumably, after Reset 8, it'll become Fall (or maybe Summer or Winter. It's not guaranteed as far I recall). Reset 7 seems to be coming up, but we'll see.

posts.content_html_raw:
My first time playing Lessons in Love was December 13, 2020. One week before that, randomly browsing through itch.io, I had picked about five games on a whim, LiL included (I saw a picture of depressed Rin, which piqued my interest.) For the following one and a half years, I kept downloading the public builds released on Itch every month. At that time, I didn't know this site existed. Shortly before joining here, LiL was removed/blocked from Itch temporarily (due to some ethics org's complaints or something.) Wanting to know what happened, I stumbled upon this thread, registered, and was exposed to many great games. I'm thankful.

I also didn't read the description and thought it was a standard dating sim (this was another pleasant surprise, as I've always enjoyed denpa.)
