I am so hyped for Reset 7... Like Reset 6 from update 0.35, this one will also fall on a Halloween. Judging from all the buildup we're getting with the TSS events and also Nodoka hinting at these 'gateways' to other existential planes, I agree when you say it will be a wild experience.

My biggest curiosity of all right now is what role New Maya will play in this. She's able to listen to conversations regarding false memories and timeloops without forcefully interrupting, so it's clear she still has the potential to make it to the rooftop... She's simply ignorant right now, similar to Akira at the very start of the game.

Assuming Maya sticks around for the apocalypse this time, though, just as Chapter 1 Sensei did, there's no way that ignorance can last for too much longer. She'll have no choice but to reconsider certain aspects of what she's been told.

Also Also: this will be the first ever Springtime Reset... So naturally I'm terrified yet intrigued for what is to come.

I've held this unpopular opinion for way too long, but I like the Reset puzzles. XD It makes you feel as though you've accomplished something and actively fought back against your (Akira's) slowly deteriorating mind. I enjoy all the weird and random shit we get to see during the puzzles. Times New Roman was a slog, I agree. And the coffee questions were really stupid. But the music? The visuals of the room? The haunting implications that this is a potential future where Akira just stayed in his room? Love that shit.

Bring on the puzzles, Sel! I'm prepared.

Tl;dr - I might be a little hyped for Reset 7. Just a little bit.

Well, this one is more interesting because (Deskel will correct me if I am mwrong) we have to sacrifice something of equal value in order to return her; so her presence in TSS events is an actual promise of something horrible. We also don't known how much of abomination she will be when she will return; and I honestly expect that Sensei would regret bringing her back.

Also, her return would likely mean the end of a new Maya, which would also be the drama I wish to see. And Chinami will just return back with some memories possibly erased. Boring
Click to expand...
It's not clear, but Kaori's explanation of wishes, stories, faceless elves, and gold stars, may be a hint at how to bring Maya Prime back. Ami seemed to want to use whatever wishes or gold stars that she's got (if any) to bring the moon back:
Sensei - "What would you use your gold star on, Ami?"
Ami - "I'd like to bring the moon back, I think."
Presumably, her mother is this moon (could be Maya, but I don't think Ami wants Maya Prime back), however SeKaori seemed to say that changing the past would lead to notable consequences of equal or greater value:
Kaori - "Putting the moon back will be rewriting history. And such a thing can not be done without consequences of equal or greater value."
(Chapter 4 Kaori 'Il Cervo' Event)
So, if Maya Prime does come back, in a similar way, it will likely have consequences of relative value, as well.

However, Pareidolia seemed to imply it'd bring Maya Prime back if Sensei raped Karin in Karin's 'Paranoid' Chapter 4 Event, and suggested that something else could maybe give Sensei a miracle and bring her back in Chapter 4's 'The Collector' Main Event, then Pareidolia suggested that following It is the only way to get his "girl" back, but was purposely vague about which "girl" in Chapter 4's 'On the Count of Three' Main Event.

(Of course, Pareidolia might just be talking out of it's "not even real" ass)

Overall: There is a possibility of Maya Prime's return, but it's not all that clear on what the cost might be, or how it'd work exactly.

Comiies said:
What do you guys think is the best event in the game?
Click to expand...
“The End of the Tour (Glasswalker)” is my favorite event in Lessons in Love. Where Akira remembers more of his past with Niki, has to face what happened with the car accident, and (re)learns his name. Really that entire Niki event chain was fucking amazing. I can’t praise it enough.

Honorable mentions include: “I Will Deliver You to the Fireflies”, where Akira professes his love for Maya and leads to one of the most emotional and visually stunning scenes of the game.

“There Is A Light That Never Goes Out” for the wholesome Ami content and having her relationship with Sensei evolve into more of a father/daughter relationship.

And also “Spotless Mind” from Christmas 2, purely for the sequence where Akira is back in the past and views a childhood memory with Niki thanks to Wires. “memories.mp3” is such a good song. It always impacts me when it plays… Really it was this event in particular that made me go from invested in Lessons in Love to “I’m obsessed now, aren’t I?”

Comiies said:
Also your assertion made me think.What do you guys think is the best event in the game? There is no specific criteria.It can be for pure wholesomeness like The color white(Which is also my fav event) or it can be filled to the brimm with lore.
Click to expand...
I'm a sucker for when books or chapters end on a line that abruptly adds something significant. Like answering a question or tying the loose ends of a theme.

There are so many good events to choose from but one I think about a lot is "Zanzibar (Counting Cats)". It's probably not a critically important event but I just like it. Now is a great time to talk about it given what next update might bring.

It's the final part in the Chika onsen event chain. Sensei wakes up early and begins monologueing to quell his boredom. He brings up a quote from Thoreau which is where the event gets it's name.

The scene is an intimate and comfortable moment. Chika finally wakes up. They talk for a bit and the conversation leads to chika mentioning his status as boyfriend, which Sensei doesn't have the heart to dispute.

The cats in Zanzibar aren't relevant again until the very end of the event.
As Sensei waits outside for Chika to finish talking to Tsubasa, he starts thinking about Tsubasa sexually. And then onto how to maintain his expanding harem which is immediately interrupted by the final line.

As Sensei alluded to, the line from Thoreau isn't about being lazy. It's about inward reflection. Criticizing people who literally travel abroad and fail to find happiness when the real answer is focusing on themselves.

Sensei is a miserable person. He travels from person to person, hoping their affections will make him feel something. But he remains miserable. Perhaps, the answer is to stay in Zanzibar. Focus on a relationship you already have and develop that.

Chika, partly due to naivete, is always trying to develop a good relationship. She's shown throughout the game to be reflective, analyzing how she might be a better partner. You can even see that in this very event.
But Chika largely hasn't been tested or trusted. She hasn't had to deal with Sensei's black-outs, his past, or any of the supernatural stuff. However, that doesn't mean she can't. We don't know because Sensei never lets her in. Not just Chika, Sensei never lets anyone in until they have to be.
Chika is counting the cats in Zanzibar while Sensei continues to run away from every relationship. Afraid of commitment that could be built into the sustainable happiness he needs.

Click to expand...
Oh, and I think I may be alone in this one, but I love the event with the japanese name (including the soundtrack), commonly referred to as "Sekai's restoration". I've loved it since the second replay though, and that's because I interpret it as "Akira's restoration" rather than Sekai's. Himawari (?) says in the event before it that "it can be beautiful to see something die in fragments, but it's even more beautiful to see it restored". And that is what LiL is about for me.

The whole ending up like her mother, and her trying to liberate everyone stuff from last update:
Nodoka - "I can't...end up like her! I can't! I won't I...NGAAAAH! FUCK YOU, BRAIN! FUCK YOU, GOD! YOU CAN'T...HIDE...FOREVER!!!!"
- "Everything...I do...NGAAAAAH! It's all...to break the mold!...To liberate us!"
(Chapter 4 Nodoka 'Mille Crepe' Event)

Nodoka - "To get back on track, the reason I'm making this a 'condition' is that I've been quite worried about Otoha's well-being lately."
(Chapter 2 'Yuritopia' Main Event)
- "The best thing for you is to truly experience freedom. And to do that, you must escape the cage."
(Chapter 2 'Birdcage' Main Event)

- "So if she even thinks about hurting you again, she'll have to hurt me first."
(Chapter 2 Yumi 'See You Around' Event)
Etc.

(Chapter 2 Nodoka 'Coloring Book' Event)
- "I need to figure out how to make all of you understand."
- "If I can't, my existence means nothing."
(Chapter 3 Nodoka 'Amoeba (Incontrovertible Peculiarity)' Event)

(Chapter 3's 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event) That's seemingly Nodoka being drowned in the Library/Wishing Well.

She's definitely in my top 10, though. Anyone who actually hates her...well, I see them as the crazy ones, lmao. Kind of pity them as well.

posts.content_html_raw:
aramaug said:
Jesus Christ, and I thought DeSkel was a psychopath for liking Nodoka.
Click to expand...
Lmao, look, it's not like i love it cause it got my dick hard or something, i love it because it was powerful, that it had an impact on me. It was awful to witness, but it wasn't awful in its construction, it was extremely well done and i'm not someone that needs something to put a smile on my face for me to find it beautiful.

Don't get me wrong, i understand why most people might look at what i said and wonder wtf is wrong with me, but remember, this is fiction, as a species we use fiction to explore what could be, what might be, and also what we wish never was. I'm never ever going to want to hear a real story that mirrors Io's, i couldn't stomach it, literally, even imagining the concept as i type this has my stomach churning, but to safely explore it through fiction, well done fiction at that... it's a gift, one i am thankful for, one that adds greater depth to my experience as a thinking consciousness in this ridiculously absurdist universe.

Stomachache had an impact on me and it's one i will remember many many times in the future. I love it for that; the older i get, the rarer and rarer such experiences come upon me, i'm a misanthropic lump of jaded humanoid flesh, so anything that make me feel something real is something of tremendous value to me.

I know this is a subject that has been kind of beaten to death, but I don't think I've shared my own take on it yet, even if it overlaps a lot with what others have said. Warning: wall of text incoming.
First of all I think that we need to separate enjoying Nodoka as a character from liking Nodoka as a person. I think the first of those is very defensible; at one point, she might have been borderline top ten for me as a character (but not anymore, see below). On the other hand, I do think you have to be kind of crazy to think that Nodoka is anything other than the worst person among all of the non-Sensei characters.

On Nodoka as a person:
  • She's constantly sexually harassing people and has committed sexual assault on multiple occasions.
  • She views everyone other than the few people that she "cares" about as nothing more than toys that she's free to do whatever she wants with.
  • Even for the people she "cares" about, she thinks she's the sole arbiter of what's best for them and that they should be grateful for what she does, no matter their own feelings.
  • I'm putting "cares" in quotes because she herself says she only cares about people she's interested in, so all of her friendships have ulterior motives (Futaba because of the upside down house; Otoha because of her sexual proclivities and connection to Sekai; Sensei because of, well, everything).
  • When Sensei is trying to be a better person in Chapter 3, she actively pushes him to regress and start using people again, arguing that the two of them transcend morality because they're special or some bullshit.
  • Uniquely among all of the people in the game who do bad things, she never expresses the least bit of remorse, guilt, or desire to improve the way she treats people.
  • She's incredibly smug in her own intelligence and refuses to admit the possibility of being wrong.
  • That fucking smirk.
Because Selebus is a good writer, she has a backstory that explains how she came to be the person she is and has consistent motivations, but that doesn't excuse being a complete piece of shit, just like how Yumi's bullying and Io's misogyny aren't justified by their own experiences.

In terms of Nodoka as a character, I usually think she's pretty interesting. Her perspective is unique and it's enjoyable to try to understand how she sees the world, even if the result is absolutely vile. But especially on my second playthrough, the way that Selebus tries to show her intelligence has been really grating:
  • Being able to recite memorized facts (especially the truly trivial details that she does) has so little correlation with intelligence that it's laughable.
  • Despite being a sociopath with zero empathy, we're supposed to believe that she understands people well enough to perfectly manipulate them without ever misjudging their response. For example, knowing that Yumi won't just fucking murder her, or knowing that a very specific series of actions will lead to Rin and Otoha fucking.
  • Her supposedly brilliant deductions about the world and peoples' pasts are at best based on clues that we're not privy to, so they just come across as omniscience.
This is especially annoying because Selebus is able to write actually smart characters. With characters like Noriko, Ayane, and Io, we actually see them being smart by doing things like reading between the lines of what people say and figuring things out based on the available evidence. Maybe he feels he can't do this with Nodoka because she lacks emotional intelligence (but then why is she so effective at manipulating people?) or maybe he thinks he needs to go further because she's presented as being so far above everyone else, but then the wheels fall off.

I'm still holding out hope that it will be revealed that all of her information is actually being fed to her by a third party, like the voices in her head or the whispers of the world, and her intelligence really is a form of omniscience. But in 0.42 we have everyone once again proclaiming her a genius for figuring things out on her own, and it feels like that's also what Selebus wants us to think as readers. I hope I'm wrong.

I'm also really annoyed by how Selebus uses her as a self insert in the book plot so that he can talk about how amazing he is as a writer and basically berate his own readers for approaching things wrong and for liking Sensei as a character despite the awful shit he does. I find this to be the most insufferable of all of his fourth wall breaks because it's so self-aggrandizing.

Uniquely among all of the people in the game who do bad things, she never expresses the least bit of remorse, guilt, or desire to improve the way she treats people.
She's incredibly smug in her own intelligence and refuses to admit the possibility of being wrong.
That fucking smirk.
Because Selebus is a good writer, she has a backstory that explains how she came to be the person she is and has consistent motivations, but that doesn't excuse being a complete piece of shit, just like how Yumi's bullying and Io's misogyny aren't justified by their own experiences.
In terms of Nodoka as a character, I usually think she's pretty interesting. Her perspective is unique and it's enjoyable to try to understand how she sees the world, even if the result is absolutely vile. But especially on my second playthrough, the way that Selebus tries to show her intelligence has been really grating:
Being able to recite memorized facts (especially the truly trivial details that she does) has so little correlation with intelligence that it's laughable.
Despite being a sociopath with zero empathy, we're supposed to believe that she understands people well enough to perfectly manipulate them without ever misjudging their response. For example, knowing that Yumi won't just fucking murder her, or knowing that a very specific series of actions will lead to Rin and Otoha fucking.
Her supposedly brilliant deductions about the world and peoples' pasts are at best based on clues that we're not privy to, so they just come across as omniscience.
This is especially annoying because Selebus is able to write actually smart characters. With characters like Noriko, Ayane, and Io, we actually
see
them being smart by doing things like reading between the lines of what people say and figuring things out based on the available evidence. Maybe he feels he can't do this with Nodoka because she lacks emotional intelligence (but then why is she so effective at manipulating people?) or maybe he thinks he needs to go further because she's presented as being so far above everyone else, but then the wheels fall off.
I'm still holding out hope that it will be revealed that all of her information is actually being fed to her by a third party, like the voices in her head or the whispers of the world, and her intelligence really is a form of omniscience. But in 0.42 we have everyone once again proclaiming her a genius for figuring things out on her own, and it feels like that's also what Selebus wants us to think as readers. I hope I'm wrong.
I'm also really annoyed by how Selebus uses her as a self insert in the book plot so that he can talk about how amazing he is as a writer and basically berate his own readers for approaching things wrong and for liking Sensei as a character despite the awful shit he does. I find this to be the most insufferable of all of his fourth wall breaks because it's so self-aggrandizing.

Lurking here, it seems like everyone accepts that Ayane lost her pregnancy. The evidence that himawari is her daughter is pretty strong, but what is the evidence that she was ever pregnant during the course of the game?
Click to expand...
There are numerous hints, actually. Mainly from Ayane. But I've compiled probably the most obvious bits of evidence.


Ayane - "Sensei...even though she's beautiful...remember who it is that's carrying your child."
*Transition*
Ayane - "And...umm...Sensei-"
- "If you wouldn't mind, I'd like to maybe talk to you about something soon."
- "If that's okay."

Event name: "She's Always a Woman" (Chapter 2 Sara Event)


Ayane - "Sensei! It's Ayane! Your favorite student and soon to be mother of your children!"

Event name: "Let Me Die in Spring" (Chapter 2 Main Event)


Sensei - "If you pull the pregnancy trick on me again, I swear-"
Ayane - "Are you really that afraid of becoming a daddy?"
Sensei - "Yes. Now tell me what this is really about."
Ayane - "..."
- "So...umm...remember how I said I might need some more attention soon?"
*Transition*
Ayane - "Sensei.."
- "Something..."
- "Something happened and..."
- "And it's something I really need your help with and..."
Sensei - "..."
Ayane - "..."
- "Nevermind."

Event name: "Nevermind" (Chapter 2 Ayane Event)



*Post Reset 3 where Ayane made it to the roof the first time, but disappeared*
Ayane - "The truth is...I tried to sleep, but..."
- "But I had this really weird dream."
- "A dream that I...can't quite remember anymore."
- "And...when I woke up..."
- "I felt like I'd lost something."
- "Something really, really important to me and...and I couldn't even put my finger on what it was."
*Transition*
Sensei Narrator - "Huh."
- "I feel like I may have lost something too."

Event name: "Before the Sun Comes Up" (Chapter 2 Ayane Event)


Himawari Narrator - "Right now, a girl is lost in the woods."
- "And while there are a million other things she should be worrying about-"
- "While there are a trillion other things she should be worrying about-"
- "What she wants is all too simple."
- "What she wants is her mother."
*Transition*
Himawari - "Now, what's a beautiful girl like you doing wandering around the woods in the middle of the night?"
Ayane - "Who..."
- "Why?..." (Begins to cry harder upon sensing Himawari's familiarity.)
*Transition*
Himawari Narrator - "She found her." (As in she found her mother, Ayane.)

Event name: "Fairytale (The End Until Tomorrow)" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

Still not enough? Take a hint from Himawari too:


Sensei - "Then, for the sake of ending this extremely weird conversation on a good note...can you tell me your name?"
Himawari - "..."
Sensei - "..."
Himawari - "Why don't you give me one?"
- "Name me after your favorite flower."

Event name: "Ad Meliora" (Chapter 3 Sana Event)


Himawari - "But for now, I'll close myself up and wait for the light to shine once more."
- "Forever yours--"
- "Your little sunflower."

Event name: "Flowerchild" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

Among other examples listed by other users who type way faster than I do, because holy hell this is touched on a lot in the game if you really think about it. It becomes even more clear on a repeat playthrough since you have additional context.

Click to expand...
I'd think it's technically possible, though it'd be kind of a twist that we're not given huge clues to predict. Depending on how you view/accept the human soul/spirit and whether or not one certain interpretation of that applies to the LiL universe — or if you want to view Himawari as a Schrodinger's cat stand-in as I've put it before — I think any first-born child Ayane has could just be Himawari. Especially in a time-loop setting. Himawari would just be the soul/person that is to be Ayane's child, if that makes sense. Through the first two chapters, Akira would always get weird around the topic of pregnancy. When Ami talks about being inseminated, Akira gets up and walks out mid-coitus. When Ayane is laying the foundation to drop news of the pregnancy on him, he threatens to push her off the roof if she talks about being pregnant again.

It was so bad that I had suspected for quite some time that the real reason the loops are happening is because Maya had told him she was pregnant with his child, and he promptly jumped off the roof, and that's the leap that starts the game. Indeed, that was the core impetus behind the entire "Maya is pregnant" theory (that and the way she eats).

The only other reason I can think of for his reaction being so visceral is that maybe Sekai was pregnant when she died. Either way, something is definitely up with the way he has such a complex about pregnancy in the first half of the game (though that aspect of his personality definitely seems to have mellowed by chapter 4)

posts.content_html_raw:
Yumi didn’t deserve what she got in “Matador” and “Things That Hurt”. But at the same time, Futaba didn’t deserve to be bullied by Yumi for so many years. Yumi was really awful towards her and was likely the sole reason for her bulimia problem to start with.

That said, Nodoka went way too far. That’s not just revenge, it is a series of crimes. And despite Yumi being able to walk away from it in one of the paths, that’s entirely dependent on if she knows about Sensei’s relationship with Chika or not. Obviously the Yumi on the other path is gonna give in to the blackmail, because she’s afraid of hurting her best friend who likes the same guy she does and she’s the only family she has.

I don’t blame Yumi for screaming “I’ll kill you” to Nodoka when beating the shit out of her either. The fuck else was she meant to say after being mentally scarred?

You know what they say: “Two wrongs don’t make a right.” Yumi was wrong for bullying Futaba and Nodoka was wrong for sexually assaulting her and roping Sensei into the mix too.

To play devil’s advocate for Nodoka for a moment, though, I think she’s way too overhated. Like okay sure, the Yumi thing didn’t earn her any points, but as we’ve learned… most of what she does, she does not out of malice, but as a way to shape the world herself.

Just look at what happened after she outed Io’s backstory in front of everyone. It made Io uncomfortable, but will ultimately over time be able to move her forward. You can even compare this to Tsuneyo’s standup routine in Dorm Wars 2. It served the exact same purpose.

Even last update, where Nodoka caught on to a lot of aspects about their world, including the time loops and gateways between existential planes.

Nodoka’s fucking weird and polarizing, but also interesting.

Imo Otoha is a way more hatable character. Her betrayal of Rin multiple times and her annoyingly aloof demeanor never fails to get a lip smack out of me.

Chika’s the one who summed it up best:

Wow, that joke on DeSkel blew up out of proportion didn't it? There are way too many replies so I'll just sum it up without linking a specific one:
DeSkel is absolutely correct that things really go down in a later event, not Matador (although they're linked). However, aramaug and the others that pointed out that Matador is still way more than everyday bullying are also correct.

That Yumi can reject the blackmail/sexual assault does not lessen it, as someone could say they'd shoot me if I didn't do something, and then you can't really use as justification that in an alternate timeline where I said no anyway, they didn't shoot me afterwards - as that clearly wasn't what was presented to the victim.

Regarding the "I'm not paying enough attention" comment, that was also obviously a joke guys (at least I took it this way) - but if we were to take it seriously, then I'd say that sexual assault includes the attempt to force someone to do something sexual against their will. To say that there is no sexual assault/harrasment in Matador is ignorant towards its basic definition.

Lastly, DeSkel didn't say it was everyday bullying, he said it was bullying - that was an exaggeration on my part as to make the joke. And well, it is bullying, just as if there is a physical assault that ends in a homicide, it is still a physical assault (although I would call it by the heavier part of the act if summing it up).
Final note, I consider myself friends enough with DeSkel that I can poke fun at him/be poked back regarding our perspectives towards LiL.
